title: Ruff v. Nashville Presbytery
disposition_detail: Judgment on two issues: (1) inadequate BCO 31-2 investigation—Yes; (2) failure to find a strong presumption of guilt on the evidence—Yes. The complaint was sustained and remanded to Nashville Presbytery for further proceedings consistent with the opinion (BCO 43-10). The separate complaint assertion that the August 4 letter was an inadequate private response was not separately answered. The concurrence concurred only in the remand result, not the majority rationale.
first_summary: The SJC sustained Matt Ruff's complaint that Nashville Presbytery failed adequately to investigate alleged offenses by TE George Grant and failed to find a strong presumption of guilt. It held the investigation record incomplete and contradictory and remanded for further proceedings. A concurrence agreed only in the remand.
summary: Nashville Presbytery's BCO 31-2 investigation of reports against TE George Grant was inadequately documented and internally inconsistent, and the evidence before Presbytery raised a strong presumption of guilt, the SJC held. It sustained the complaint, ruling that pastoral reconciliation does not displace the duty to institute judicial process, and remanded for further proceedings; it did not adjudicate Grant guilty. A concurrence agreed only in remanding to supplement the record under BCO 42-5 & 7.

sources.supports: Identity, procedural history, issues, judgment, adopted reasoning, disposition, concurrence, and adoption vote.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: Case 2009-28, Ruff v. Nashville Presbytery; SJC, 39th GA (2011); proposed panel decision by TE Howie Burkhalter amended and adopted by panel and full SJC; 20 concurred, 1 disqualified, 3 absent (lines 1–3, 148–156; pp. 567, 573).
evidence_notes.dispute: Matt Ruff complained that Nashville Presbytery failed adequately to investigate July 2008 reports about TE George Grant and wrongly found no chargeable offenses; his Sept. 9, 2009 complaint was denied Nov. 10, 2009, then taken to GA (lines 13–38; pp. 567–569).
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: Both issues answered Yes; complaint sustained and remanded. The adopted opinion held the BCO 31-2 investigation was inadequately documented and internally inconsistent and that evidence raised a strong presumption of guilt requiring process; pastoral reconciliation did not excuse judicial duty (lines 42–56, 58–144; pp. 569–573).
evidence_notes.qualifications: Concurring opinion agreed only in remand to supplement the record under BCO 42-5 & 7, not the majority rationale; it noted BCO 34 discretion over seriousness and lacked specific allegations (lines 158–174; pp. 573–574). The prior May 11, 2009 complaint is not the matter before the SJC (line 21; p. 567).
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: No separate incorporated decision; the adopted SJC decision and concurrence are in this source.

score_reasons.concrete_dispute: Identifies the challenged Presbytery actions: inadequate BCO 31-2 investigation and failure to find a strong presumption of guilt on reports about Grant.
score_reasons.decision: States both issues answered Yes, complaint sustained, remand, and concurrence limited to remand.
score_reasons.decisive_reason: Explains adopted reasons: incomplete and internally inconsistent investigation record and evidence raising strong presumption; pastoral duty does not displace judicial process.
score_reasons.distinctive_value: Preserves the rule that BCO 31-2 investigations must be documented and that strong presumption requires process; notes no guilt adjudication and concurrence rationale.
